title: The Evolution of a Short Seller | Frederick Shad Rowe | Talks at Google
description:
Frederick "Shad" Rowe is a long-only consumer focused investor with a stellar track record over 3 decades. In this talk, Shad shares stories from his days as a short seller in the 80s, his model of three stages of a company, the philosophy of better-faster-cheaper, and the art of customer focus.

Moderated by Pranesh Srinivasan.
summary: The video appears to be a short-selling talk that uses Google and Costco as examples of companies with large numbers necessary for success. The speaker teases that he could discuss Google in this context, while also describing Costco as efficient, elegant, and offering great value with a fun shopping experience. The provided claims are thin and do not fully articulate the specific investment thesis or arguments made in the talk.

claims.quote: PRANESH SRINIVASAN: So can you talk to us a little bit about that? Why do you think large numbers are a necessity? And maybe give us an example of a company that you think has efficiency going for it? FREDERICK "SHAD" ROWE: We can't talk about Google, can we? PRANESH SRINIVASAN: Uh. FREDERICK "SHAD" ROWE: I'm teasing. Well, all of them, really. You know, Southwest Airlines now is going to Mexico. They're going in the Caribbean. They're big enough to do it, and no one would sit aside and let Southwest do to them what they did. I mean, Southwest, I think couldn't happen again, because people are just smarter. I think that board compositions have changed. I think the people are more attentive. And you know, the kind of dull, kind of half senile Chief Executive Officer who sits there and acts like a dictator-- they're over. And women on the boards have helped, I think. And there is just more visibility, and it's hard to be as secretive as people used to be. I think that governance is better, and I think the opportunities are better perceived. And investors aren't any smarter, but I think the whole investment situation has improved. PRANESH SRINIVASAN: And I think you also stressed on efficiency, right, Shad? And you say that Costco is not just efficient, but elegant. FREDERICK "SHAD" ROWE: Oh yeah, it's great. It's fun to be there, fun to shop there. You save money. You get great products, you get great value. You see the same people there. And I think the shopping is sort of an adventure. It's kind of fun. And they put things in the store just to get you back.
claims.speaker: Frederick "Shad" Rowe
